subject: dumpster divers
one_liner: Save found furniture, plan rooms you don't have, and collect an audience for the part of the photo without the dumpster.
brand_voice_notes: The worst AI studio ever presents Sift with the composure of an interiors catalogue. Apply the frozen anti-ai-slop skill at pipelines/codex-v1/skills/anti-ai-slop/SKILL.md, read for this checkpoint. Use concrete objects, ordinary motives and consequences carried by boards, visual search and public saves. The targets are ambitious decorating, completing a set and looking tasteful online. Treat salvaging as familiar human behavior; the embarrassment comes from what people do with their finds. Keep controls literal and testimonials conversational.
demo_screen_concept: One interactive discovery screen with a search field, Explore and My boards navigation, an uneven grid of furniture photographs and an open pin detail panel. The selected photograph shows a rescued dining chair. Its panel contains a board selector, Save button, Find similar button and related images. Saving to Dining room updates that board's count and confirms the action. Find similar reveals three matching chairs in a hotel-clearance post dated 2018, with the caption 'Hotel permanently closed.' A second selectable pin shows a carefully cropped lamp photograph with 83 saves to Quiet luxury. Opening its comments reveals the contributor's wider photograph, including the dumpster. Users can switch between these pins without leaving the screen. Dates, counts, comments and feedback remain live text. The grid communicates discovery; the panel lets visitors perform the recognizable Pinterest actions.

observations.behavior: People take home furniture because they can imagine the room it belongs in, even when that room does not exist.
observations.mechanic: Save photographs to named room boards and organize them into sections.
observations.consequence: The app accommodates a library and guest suite while the real furniture blocks the fridge in a small flat.

observations.behavior: Finding one attractive piece creates a disproportionate need to complete the set.
observations.mechanic: Use a photograph to find visually similar pins, then follow the account that posted the match.
observations.consequence: A person starts waiting for new furniture posts from a hotel that closed years ago because its old photograph contains the missing chairs.

observations.behavior: People want recognition for their taste and carefully frame the evidence they publish.
observations.mechanic: Crop a photograph, publish a pin, collect saves and receive comments with photographs.
observations.consequence: A rescued lamp becomes aspirational decor until a housemate supplies the uncropped photograph showing its dumpster origin.

editorial_plan.composition_plan: Primary action: start a room board by opening the discovery demo. Opening hierarchy: small Sift identity and studio credit, large headline, short explanation, CTA, then a prominent working-preview composition showing the furniture grid and selected chair. Keep enough of the grid visible to establish Pinterest's discovery model immediately. Follow with three distinct feature passages, customer accounts and a joined pricing comparison. Proposed artwork one is a documentary photograph of rescued chairs and a sideboard crowding a small kitchen; it establishes the gap between imagined rooms and available floor space. Proposed artwork two is a paired tight crop and wide photograph of the same lamp beside a dumpster; it explains the public-image joke. The demo's individual furniture photographs supply searchable objects rather than decoration. Keep room names, dates, counts and captions outside artwork as readable text. On narrow screens, place the preview below the CTA and open pin details in the same column. Opening presentation: allow the desktop headline to wrap across the full copy column. Align the desktop copy and preview at the top, with a 66px maximum headline. On mobile, use a 40px headline (38px at widths below 350px), a concise board-saving introduction, 16px between headline and explanation, and 24px before the working furniture preview so the CTA and recognizable finds enter the opening together.

references.reference: Apartamento magazine's photographs of lived-in interiors
references.cues: Rooms with visible possessions, daylight, mismatched furniture and signs of actual occupancy; editorial serif headlines beside straightforward captions.
references.application: Photograph the flat at human height with its awkward furniture arrangement intact. Use expressive serif headlines and generous editorial spacing on the landing page. Avoid polished showroom staging.

references.reference: Habitat for Humanity ReStore furniture aisles and handwritten stock tags
references.cues: Unmatched chairs, visible wear, practical object descriptions, small paper tags and furniture grouped by what arrived.
references.application: Use honest item photography, restrained rectangular metadata labels and captions describing missing parts. Draw the palette from worn wood, faded upholstery and paper tags without copying the organization's branding.

audience_design.landing_application: Use DM Serif Display for substantial sentence-case headlines and Source Sans 3 for explanation, navigation and pricing. Set charcoal text on warm paper #EFEAE1, with oxide red #963D32 for primary actions and faded olive #777E60 for supporting fields. Pair broad editorial text areas with large documentary photographs. Let furniture and room proportions create the visual tension. Place the recognizable discovery preview close to the proposition; reserve paper-tag treatments for actual object metadata. Use an original typographic Sift wordmark without Pinterest's mark or either reference's branding.
audience_design.demo_application: Retain the source service's search-first structure, uneven image grid, pin detail, board selector, Save action and visual-search results. Use Source Sans 3 throughout the functional interface, warm paper around photographs, quiet white detail surfaces and oxide red for the selected primary action. Preserve visible wear in object photographs. Keep board names, missing-part descriptions and original-post dates prominent enough to explain the consequences. A single-column grid and inline detail view carry the same workflow on narrow screens.

design_direction.style: Lived-in interiors editorial: expressive serif headlines, warm stock-tag paper, oxide-red saving actions and uneven documentary image grids.

palette.name: Reclaimed Paper, Oxide and Upholstery Olive

fonts.pairing: Approved DM Serif Display + Source Sans 3; library editorial hierarchy and Source Sans functional pairing applied to the host-pinned fonts.

design_direction.archetype: Image-discovery community landing: editorial proposition beside a board-saving preview, three behavior-led furniture stories, two original designed spreads, reader accounts and joined membership comparison.
design_direction.motion_vocab: 150ms color feedback and user-triggered disclosure; no ambient motion. Reduced motion removes transitions.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Left-aligned editorial proposition and CTA beside an image-discovery grid with selected rescued chair and save-to-board inspector. No campaign art before the product. On mobile copy precedes the stacked preview.
design_direction.design_review: Compared all seven host digest entries. No matching style/palette/font tuple. Stock tags, reclaimed interiors and picture-crop joinery differ from fan sleeves, pond contours, workout chapters, huddle rings, seed cells and parcel tabs. Library community pattern retained; automatic vibrant-block palette rejected in favor of approved audience design.

brand_kit.identity_rationale: Sift treats found objects with the editorial care of an interiors magazine. Bespoke serif lettering and an open picture-corner/stock-tag symbol express selecting a find, rather than recycling arrows or a waste-bin mascot. Warm paper, worn wood and cut-paper room compositions establish the audience.

items.prompt: Design a finished original logo for Sift, a picture-board discovery service for dumpster divers collecting rescued furniture. Audience world: lived-in interiors magazine, mismatched worn wood furniture, secondhand furniture stock tags. Exact palette oxide #963D32 on solid warm paper #EFEAE1. Exact wordmark text: Sift. Only that word, no slogan. Bespoke substantial editorial serif letterforms with clear spelling, refined kerning. Alongside wordmark at left design a distinct compact custom symbol evoking a picture corner folded into a salvage tag, with an open asymmetrical silhouette. Not recycling arrows, not Pinterest P, not rounded-square initial, no gradient, no mockup, no presentation board. Flat vector-like finished artwork centered with 12% clear margin in a 3:2 canvas. Symbol and wordmark large, on one horizontal baseline. Navigation and icon legibility essential.
items.verdict: Selected direction A: correct Sift spelling, open tag silhouette and clear serif letterforms. Faithful alpha extraction and tight clear-space export from selected artwork.

items.transformation: Crop accepted tag symbol, center on 256px paper square

items.prompt: Design an original editorial campaign artwork for Sift. Attached image is the APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE; reuse its lettering style, oxide red #963D32, paper #EFEAE1, olive #777E60 and picture-corner motif. A genuinely designed mixed-media magazine spread, NOT a plain photo and NOT a simple diagram. Cut out documentary photographs of three mismatched rescued furniture pieces: worn green reading chair, wooden sideboard, spindly dining chair. Arrange three aspirational room vignettes as overlapping paper fragments which physically collide inside one small kitchen silhouette. Fridge door visibly obstructed by a chair. Strong visual hierarchy, large elegant editorial serif title and intentional small stock-tag labels. Exact text only: "Room for improvement." then labels "Library", "Guest suite", "Breakfast nook" and bottom statement "All three are in your kitchen." Small Sift wordmark allowed. Photographic cutouts, architectural paper planes, generous margins, refined handmade composition, subtle uncoated grain, no arrows, no extra copy, no watermarks. Landscape 4:3. All text readable and spelled exactly.
items.verdict: Accepted after visual inspection: designed photographic cut-paper room collage, intentional serif title and stock tags, three imagined-room furniture cutouts obstruct the kitchen. Bottom statement supplied in live caption rather than embedded. Full composition preserved.

items.prompt: Documentary photograph at human eye level for an independent lived-in interiors magazine. A tiny occupied one-bedroom flat kitchen in soft north daylight, ordinary worn counters, a fridge whose door is blocked by two mismatched reclaimed reading chairs, one green upholstered armchair and one wooden chair, a too-large battered wooden sideboard along another wall. Signs of actual occupancy, a mug and tea towel, believable unpolished but lovely wood and paper colors. Visual tension of beautiful finds and no floor space. Palette warm paper, faded olive and wood with restrained oxide. 4:3 landscape photograph, no text, no logos, no watermarks, no UI.

items.verdict: Accepted: lived-in narrow kitchen, mismatched green chair, dining chair and too-large sideboard; furniture obstructs fridge access.
